Anglo-Employment and Migration Submodel--Possible Anglo employment by industry is calculated by subtracting Crow employment from total employment. The Anglo labor force is then compared to employment and the implied unemployment rate is calculated. If the unemployment rate (relative to the national rate) is outside of a pre-specified normal range, migration is assumed to occur to bring the rate within the normal range. The in-migrants (out-migrants) are then added (subtracted) to the base population then population, labor force and employment are once again calculated. Once the unemployment rate falls within the normal range, the iterations stop, and the model proc eds to the income submodel.
Income Submodel--Once employment by industry is calculated for both the Crow and the Anglo residents of the Impact Area, non-agricultural labor income is estimated by multiplying employment by earnings per employee.
After leaving the Income Submodel, 5 basic outputs are printed out and the model goes on to the next year.
Outputs
1. Population--Age, Sex, Race
2. Labor Force--Age, Sex, Race
3. Employment -- Race, Industry
4. Unemployment Rate--Race
5. Non-agricultural Labor Income -- Race
The inter-relationships of the five sub-models and a little more detail about the way in which their components interact is shown in the schematic representation of the model in Figure 1.
